contentBlocks.title: SASSA Grant Amounts 2026 — Complete List of All Grant Values
contentBlocks.description: See the complete list of SASSA social grant amounts for 2026 — from the SRD R370 to the Older Person Grant of R2,400 and the War Veterans Grant of R2,420. All amounts in one place for easy reference.

contentBlocks.text: Below is the complete list of SASSA social grant amounts for 2026. Amounts are reviewed annually and may increase with the national budget.

Two details matter: people aged 75 and older receive R20 more than those aged 60 to 74, and the Foster Care Grant requires a valid Children's Court order but has no income means test. Other grants have their own eligibility and means-test rules.

links.text: how the SRD differs from other grants

contentBlocks.text: There is no guaranteed extra payment every December. SASSA or government may announce one-off top-ups or additional payments, but these are not part of the regular monthly grant. Check the latest official announcement and payment schedule before budgeting for an extra amount.

contentBlocks.title: Means tests apply to some grants, not all
contentBlocks.text: Income or assets can affect eligibility or payment for grants with a means test, including the Older Person, Disability and Child Support Grants. The Foster Care Grant does not have an income means test. Check the rules for the specific grant you receive.
Grant amounts can change following a national budget or official government notice. The amounts listed above are current as of 13 November 2026.

faqs.question: Why is the SRD R370 so much less than other grants?
faqs.answer: The SRD grant is temporary relief for people who have no income and do not qualify for a full social grant. The R370 reflects that — it is meant to help, not replace a proper grant. If your circumstances change, you may qualify for a bigger grant like the Disability Grant or Child Support Grant instead.

faqs.question: Do grant amounts change every year?
faqs.answer: SASSA reviews amounts during the national budget announcement, usually in the first few months of the year. Increases are common but not guaranteed, and each grant moves separately — so stay alert rather than assuming your grant changed.

faqs.question: Will my bank charge me fees on these amounts?
faqs.answer: Any money you receive from SASSA is yours with no SASSA fee. Depending on your payment method, a retailer or bank may apply their own charges for withdrawal. The SASSA card is designed to keep withdrawal costs as low as possible.

faqs.question: Can my grant amount be less than the table shows?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you earn a little income, SASSA can pay a reduced amount based on your means test result. The table shows the maximum full amount — your actual figure can be lower if income is detected.
